Why is it that, when popular trends which are appreciated by all, suddenly become controversial when the public finds out its origin is in China? ‘K-beauty’ ‘Korean nails’ ‘Japanese makeup’, at what point do we have to realise many of those products and trends are Chinese? Or perhaps we should just be happy that it is appreciated for what it is, and not discriminated against because the public doesn’t know of its origins?

I am an ABC. I am a proud Australian. But I am also of Chinese descent. I love my ancestor’s culture and I will always defend its beauty against biased people and introduce its wonders to people who are appreciative of differences. Love your culture, and encourage others to love it too. Good luck everyone 🙏

item.desc: American Factory (2019) is a documentary about Chinese company Fuyao’s takeover of a shuttered General Motors plant in the American Rust Belt of Dayton, Ohio. As Fuyao send their own employees and laborers to work alongside the Americans, cultural differences and tensions emerge. The Chinese, with their high efficiency, strict hierarchies, and group-over-individual mindset, feel like a robotic  threat to American laborers, while ideal for American managers. Individually-minded American workers are more concerned with securing labor rights and unionizing than matching the efficiency of the Chinese. For the billionaire chairman of Fuyao, unionizing poses a threat to his profit, and the Chinese laborers are dissuaded and ultimately unable to see the value of supporting unionization.  Despite not seeing eye-to-eye at work, some Chinese and American workers find personal parallels regarding the hardship of working-class/immigrant life, emotional connection, and friendship. A standout moment was when the American management team traveled to China to observe the highly efficient Fuyao factories and attend the Fuyao employee Chinese New Year banquet. The beauty of Chinese culture moves one American to tears, and he chokes out the film’s main message, “We’re one big planet somewhat divided, but we’re one.” #documentary #chinesefilm #china #uschina #factory #factorywork #laborunion #capitalism #eastmeetswest #americanfactory #netflix #chinesenewyear #fuyao #chinesefactory #workingclass #filmanalysis

item.desc: China is one of the most regionally diverse cultures on earth. Hundreds of dialects, distinct customs, and value systems that shift province by province. And over centuries, each region developed its own reputation, its own strengths, its own identity that got passed down through generations. The Hakka were the nomads of China. Less than 10% of the population and yet they produced Sun Yat-sen, Deng Xiaoping, Lee Kuan Yew, and Tsai Ing-wen. In almost every country they settled in, they rose to the top of political power. The Cantonese were the first to leave, the first to absorb the West, and operating from a Hong Kong with creative freedoms the mainland never had, they became the tastemakers. Bruce Lee. Wong Kar-wai. Leslie Cheung. Anita Mui. They didn’t just participate in culture. They set the standard for what Chinese culture looked and sounded like for the entire world. The Hokkien built the merchant backbone of Southeast Asia before anyone was paying attention. And then they kept going. Robert Kuok. Henry Sy. Jensen Huang, who built Nvidia and the entire infrastructure of the AI revolution, born in Tainan, one of the oldest Hokkien cities in the world. Century after century, industry after industry. And Jiangnan, covering Shanghai, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu, produced the scholars. Confucian exam culture ran deepest here. That tradition didn’t disappear, it just modernized into Jack Ma, Jerry Yang, and some of the most influential tech founders of the last thirty years. These aren’t stereotypes. They’re patterns. Built over centuries of geography, migration, trade, and survival, and passed down through every generation that followed. This is why Chinese people still ask where you’re from. Your region carries a story. Your family carried it forward. Which one are you? Drop it in the comments 👇  #china #chinese #hongkong #hakka #cantonese
